newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen higher after June payroll data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen higher after June payroll data.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were expected to gain at the open on Thursday, after a key June employment report pointed to moderate growth in wages and new jobs and showed a slight increase in the unemployment rate.

"The stock market has been following interest rates and the big move in the bond market here should give the stock market a strong opening," Gail Dudack, chief investment strategist at UBS Securities said.
The Labor Department reported non-farm payrolls rose by 217,000 jobs in June versus a revised 166,000 jobs in May. The jobless rate was 5.0 percent, up from 4.8 percent.
Hourly wages rose to $12.22 per hour from $12.18 an hour in May, the government said.
The long bond soared on the data, trading up one full point at a 6.63 percent yield. The Standard & Poor's 500 futures index was up 6.40 points at 921.85.
"This is good news with respect to the Fed keeping interest rates on hold," Pierre Ellis, senior economist at Primark Decision Economist, said.

The stock market, which closes at 1300 EDT/1700 GMT today ahead of a three-day holiday in the United States, was also expected to focus on an $11.6 billion merger deal betweeen Lockheed Martin Corp and Northrop Grumman Corp.
But Guy Truicko, portfolio manager at Unity Management, said: "There are other things going on today which are more important for the overall market, like the bond market being up over a full point."
